land.text: the unified realm: Qin and the six conquered states, declared an empire in 221 BC

predecessors.note: The qin dossier (ea-01) ends at Cliopatria's 219 handoff; the real change is the 221 rename. Qin page infobox: 'Accession of Qin Shi Huang: 221 BC'.

land.text: Liu Bang's Han: 'Sichuan, Chongqing, and southern Shaanxi' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

successors.note: Bashu and Hanzhong were Qin land; granted by Xiang Yu in 206.

land.text: 'central Shaanxi and eastern Gansu', the Qin general Zhang Han
'northeastern Shaanxi', the Qin general Sima Xin
'northern Shaanxi', the Qin general Dong Yi (Kingdom of Di)
Xiang Yu's Western Chu, which already held the Chu rebels' lands of 208-207

successors.note: Xiang Yu 'then entered Xianyang' and divided the empire in 206 (Chu-Han Contention page).

capitals.name: Xianyang
capitals.note: Infobox capital: Xianyang. 'In 206 BC, Xianyang was destroyed, marking what historians consider to be the end of the imperial Qin dynasty.'

rulers.name: Qin Shi Huang (Ying Zheng)
rulers.note: Accession 221 BC (infobox); 'When Qin Shi Huang died in 210 BC, two of his advisors placed an heir on the throne.' Clipped to -218 here, the dossier's start (Cliopatria's handoff from the qin dossier); the accession year is 221.

rulers.name: Qin Er Shi (Huhai)
rulers.note: Qin page infobox: '210–207 BC: Qin Er Shi'; succession table: Er Shi Huangdi, Huhai, 210–207 BC.

rulers.name: Ziying
rulers.title: third ruler
rulers.note: 'Ziying surrendered to Liu Bang upon the latter's arrival in Xianyang in 207 BC' and 'was executed shortly thereafter by the Chu leader Xiang Yu'.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 218 shape plus Zhejiang (Kuaiji Commandery, captured 222 BC); holds 218-216

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 218-213 shape is 1,632,744 km2; the Qin infobox gives 2,300,000 km2 for 220 BC, a ratio of 0.71 (within a factor of two). The shape holds the 221 realm (it has 82 of Zhejiang's 484 grid cells) and, on this correction, holds only until 216. Zhejiang is added because the Kuaiji page says the commandery was 'captured in 222 BC' and 'ran from the south bank of the Yangtze through most of modern Zhejiang'; the minyue dossier cuts the same Zhejiang cells from Minyue. The Ordos (215) and Lingnan (214) are the later gains.

correction.text: the 218 realm, Zhejiang and the Ordos after Meng Tian's campaign

keyframe_review.note: New one-year keyframe: the Ordos is added. 'The region was conquered in 215 BC, and agriculture was established' (Qin page). Cliopatria adds only 104 of the Ordos region's 884 grid cells, and only from 212.

union.text: Lingnan: the Nanhai, Guilin and Xiang Commanderies of 214 BC, here read as Guangdong and Guangxi (not Hainan)

correction.text: Cliopatria's 210 shape plus the whole Ordos (conquered 215), Zhejiang (Kuaiji Commandery, 222) and the whole of Guangdong and Guangxi (Lingnan, 214)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 212-211 shape is an intermediate step (Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang and the Ordos edge added, Lingnan not yet). The pages date the southern conquest as one act, 214 BC ('In 214 BC, the Qin court established the Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiang Commanderies', Nanyue page), so no 212-211 step is supported: use the 214-210 shape of qin-dynasty_-210 for these years.

union.text: Lingnan: the Nanhai, Guilin and Xiang Commanderies of 214 BC, here read as Guangdong and Guangxi (not Hainan)

correction.text: Cliopatria's 210 shape plus the whole Ordos (conquered 215), Zhejiang (Kuaiji Commandery, 222) and the whole of Guangdong and Guangxi (Lingnan, 214); holds 214-210 (it replaces the 212-211 step, and covers 214-213)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 210-209 shape is 2,132,724 km2 against the infobox's 2,300,000 km2 for 220 BC (ratio 0.93; the infobox date is before the southern conquest). It is the realm after the 214 conquests, so it holds from 214 to 210, not from 210; the correction adds the whole Ordos, Zhejiang and all of Guangdong and Guangxi (Cliopatria has 54 percent of Guangdong and 6 percent of Guangxi). The Qin page quotes Brian Lander that 'Qin only had administrative control over a few areas south of the Yangzi River', so the south stays a soft edge.

union.text: Lingnan: the Nanhai, Guilin and Xiang Commanderies of 214 BC, here read as Guangdong and Guangxi (not Hainan)

minus.text: Cliopatria's 210 shape plus the whole Ordos (conquered 215), Zhejiang (Kuaiji Commandery, 222) and the whole of Guangdong and Guangxi (Lingnan, 214)

correction.text: the 214-210 realm without the lands of the Yan rebels (Han Guang)

keyframe_review.note: New one-year keyframe: Yan is lost. 'A popular revolt broke out in 209 BC'; the yan dossier (ea-01, Han Guang page) dates Yan's revival to 209. Everything else Cliopatria still draws as Qin.

correction.text: the Qin remnant of 208-207: Cliopatria's row labelled Zhai, without northern Zhejiang (Kuaiji), which Xiang Liang held for the rebel Chu from 209

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 208-207: Cliopatria draws the Qin remnant (1,628,171 km2) under the Name 'Zhai' (zhai_-208, which shares Wikidata Q7183 with this row); the Kingdom of Zhai of Dong Yi began in 206 and was 'northern Shaanxi' only. Western Chu, Jibei-labelled Shandong, Dai-labelled Hebei, Yan, Wei and Han have left by 208. Northern Zhejiang is taken out because Xiang Liang held Kuaiji for the rebel Chu from 209 (Kuaiji page); Cliopatria draws it as Qin.

region.text: the unified realm of 221, capital Xianyang

ledger.note: 218: the Qin empire enters the map under its own row. 'This culminated in 221 BC with the successful unification of China under Emperor Qin'; infobox 'Accession of Qin Shi Huang: 221 BC'. Cliopatria's Qin Dynasty row starts in 218, so the declaration of 221 is the rename event of the qin dossier and this dossier starts at the handoff.

region.text: the Ordos Desert, taken from the Xiongnu

ledger.note: 215: Meng Tian conquers the Ordos. 'In retaliation, a military campaign was led by the Qin general Meng Tian. The region was conquered in 215 BC, and agriculture was established'; the Great Wall was begun 'to protect against nomadic invasions'. Cliopatria shows only part of the Ordos, and only from 212.

region.text: Lingnan: the Nanhai, Guilin and Xiang Commanderies of 214 BC, here read as Guangdong and Guangxi (not Hainan)

ledger.note: 214: Qin completes the conquest of Lingnan. 'In 214 BC, the Qin court established the Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiang Commanderies' after Tu Sui's 500,000-man army ('around 218 BC') and the 214 reinforcements of Ren Xiao and Zhao Tuo; the Qin page says the armies 'conquered the coastal lands surrounding Guangzhou, and took the provinces of Fuzhou and Guilin'. The commanderies are named; Guangdong and Guangxi is the researcher's reading of them. The land was held by tribes, not a state.

region.text: the lands Cliopatria adds to Qin between its 218 and 210 shapes

ledger.note: 214: the rest of the southern and northern gains. 'In 214 BC, Qin Shi Huang secured his boundaries to the north with a fraction (roughly 100,000 men) of his large army, ...sent the majority (500,000 men) of his army to conquer the territory to their south.' The page names no province for these moves. The region is what Cliopatria adds to its 218 shape in its 212 and 210 shapes (Hunan, Jiangxi, Hubei, northern Shanxi and Shaanxi, the Fujian edge, Guangdong): the year is the page's, the land is Cliopatria's. Lander, quoted on the page, holds that 'Qin only had administrative control over a few areas south of the Yangzi River'.

region.text: Minyue's land in Fujian, the Minzhong Commandery

ledger.note: 214: Qin takes Minyue's land. The same 214 campaign 'took the provinces of Fuzhou and Guilin'; the Nanyue page adds that Qin 'attacked the Minyue, defeating them and establishing the Minzhong Commandery' and deposed the ruler Wuzhu, without a year. Minyue's Cliopatria shape stays in the record as occupied (the minyue dossier carries the matching event).

region.text: the Yan lands in Hebei and Liaoning

ledger.note: 209: the revolt costs Qin the north-east. 'A popular revolt broke out in 209 BC' and 'men from all over China revolted' (Qin page); the page names no rebel king. Cliopatria's Yan row holds the land from 208 (the yan dossier dates Han Guang's revival to 209 from its own page). Page silent on the region.

region.text: the Huai and lower Yangtze lands of the rebel Chu, with Kuaiji

ledger.note: 208: the rebel Chu is set up on the lost land. 'In 208 BC, Xiang Liang installed Mi Xin as King Huai II of Chu'; Xiang Liang had taken Kuaiji in 209 ('its governor Yin Tong initiated a plot to rebel against the collapsing Qin', Kuaiji page) and the Dazexiang page has Chen Sheng declared king of the former Chu in 209. The land is Cliopatria's Western Chu 208 shape plus northern Zhejiang.
208: Wei is restored on Qin's former Wei land. Page silent on Wei; the wei dossier (ea-01) dates the restoration to 208 from the Wei Bao page. The land is Cliopatria's Wei 208 shape.
208: Hán is restored. Page silent; the han dossier (ea-01) dates Han Cheng's enthronement to 208. The land is Cliopatria's Han 208 shape (4,000 km2).

region.text: Zhao Xie's Zhao in central Hebei

ledger.note: 208: the Zhao line is restored in central Hebei under Zhao Xie. Page silent on Zhao; the Battle of Julu page (opened for the dai dossier) has Zhao Xie retreating to Julu in 207. Cliopatria draws this land under the Name 'Dai' (dai_-208).

208: Shandong leaves Qin. Page silent on Qi; Cliopatria draws the whole of Shandong under the Name 'Jibei' (jibei_-208), which is really the revived Qi (Jibei was made only in 206). The qi dossier has no shape for 208-207.
207: Qin's hold on Minyue ends with the dynasty. No page dates the end of the Minzhong Commandery; the minyue dossier has the end at 206 (confidence 1 there too).

region.text: the Qin remnant of 208-207: Cliopatria's row labelled Zhai, without northern Zhejiang (Kuaiji), which Xiang Liang held for the rebel Chu from 209

ledger.note: 207: Ziying surrenders to Liu Bang and the Qin ends. 'Ziying surrendered to Liu Bang upon the latter's arrival in Xianyang in 207 BC'; he was 'executed shortly thereafter by the Chu leader Xiang Yu'; 'In 206 BC, Xianyang was destroyed' and the former Qin territories were 'temporarily divided into the Eighteen Kingdoms'. The Chu-Han Contention page has Liu Bang's army past the last resistance at Lantian 'By October 207 BCE'; no month is given for the surrender.

wars.name: Qin campaign against the Xiongnu in the Ordos
wars.outcome: Qin victory: the Ordos was conquered in 215 BC and settled; in 214 the northern boundary was secured with about 100,000 men.
wars.note: 'In 214 BC, Qin Shi Huang secured his boundaries to the north with a fraction (roughly 100,000 men) of his large army, ...sent the majority (500,000 men) of his army to conquer the territory to their south.'

wars.name: Qin conquest of Lingnan

zones.text: Lingnan: the Nanhai, Guilin and Xiang Commanderies of 214 BC, here read as Guangdong and Guangxi (not Hainan)

wars.outcome: Qin victory after a defeat: Tu Sui was killed, the 214 reinforcements prevailed and the Nanhai, Guilin and Xiang Commanderies were set up; Zhao Tuo later founded Nanyue (204).
wars.note: The Nanyue page gives 'around 218 BC' for the first army and 214 for the second; the Qin page gives 214 only.

wars.name: Dazexiang Uprising
belligerents: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang's rebels
wars.outcome: Crushed after five months by Zhang Han's army; it set the example for the rebellions that followed.
wars.note: Infobox 'August or September 209 BC'; the lead says August 209 to January 208. No territorial result is on the page.

wars.name: Rebellions against the Qin and the fall of the dynasty

zones.text: the six rebel lands of 208 as Cliopatria draws them

wars.outcome: The rebel states took about a quarter of the empire; Ziying surrendered to Liu Bang in 207 and Xiang Yu divided the empire in 206.
wars.note: 'Although the Dazexiang uprising had failed, other rebellions erupted consecutively over the next three years.'

wars.name: Battle of Julu
wars.outcome: The Qin field army under Zhang Han was beaten at Julu in 207 BC by the rebel coalition under Xiang Yu; Zhang Han surrendered in the summer of 207.
wars.note: The relief began 'In the twelfth month of 208 BC'; the page names the battle year as 207 and the surrender as 'the summer of 207 BC'.

certainty.note: No survey or treaty line: the northern edge follows the walls and the Ordos conquest, the south is a net of garrisons (Lander, quoted on the Qin page), and the 209-207 rebel frontiers are Cliopatria's approximations.

notes: ONE STATE OR TWO: Cliopatria's rows 'Qin Dynasty' (218-209) and 'Zhai' (208-204) share Wikidata Q7183, but they are two states. Zhai's first shape (zhai_-208, 208-207, 1.63 M km2) is the Qin remnant under Qin Er Shi and Ziying, so this dossier reviews it as the new keyframe qin-dynasty_-208 and the zhai dossier marks zhai_-208 wrong; Zhai's second shape (206-204, 26,000 km2, northern Shaanxi) is the Kingdom of Zhai of Dong Yi, a separate state of the Eighteen Kingdoms (dossier zhai). The dossier starts at Cliopatria's 218 handoff from the qin dossier (real change: 221, a rename there) and ends at the 207 surrender; the Qin page's 'Destruction of Xianyang: 206 BC' is the later date some historians use. Rebel losses of 209-208 are confidence 1: no page opened names the rebel kings or lands of Zhao, Qi, Wei, Hán or Yan; the six rebel shapes of 208 (Western Chu, Yan, Wei, Han, Dai, Jibei) add up to the cells Qin loses between its 210 and 208 shapes (2,685 of 2,695 grid cells), which is what dates the loss to Cliopatria's 208. Cliopatria's Yan and Qi are not mine: counterpart 'qi' stands for the revived Qi (Shandong) of 208-207, which the qi dossier (ea-01) does not cover; counterpart 'dai' stands for Zhao Xie's Zhao. Southern gains: Cliopatria staggers them 212 and 210; the Qin and Nanyue pages date the whole conquest 214, and 214-210 is the shape used. Not on any page: the Qin infobox 'Today part of', the boundary of the Minzhong Commandery, the Ordos' boundary beyond 'the region', the month of Ziying's surrender. Pages: Qin dynasty, Nanyue, Kuaiji Commandery, Dazexiang Uprising, plus the three shared hub pages (Eighteen Kingdoms, Chu-Han Contention, Timeline of the Chu-Han Contention) read for the whole batch; 4 pages beyond the hubs against a budget of 1-2: the Nanyue and Kuaiji pages were needed to date the south (214) and Zhejiang (222), the Dazexiang page to date the revolt (209). Gazetteer: no new names (Ordos, Guangdong, Guangxi, Zhejiang resolve).
